tldr: Repeated fair assignments to a fixed bounded affine map provide exact numerical equations. For the finite-population weak-threshold rollout contrast, retaining endpoint atoms and imposing no positive margin, this note establishes a matched minimax precision surface for every block count, degree and finite replay count. The risk has order \((1+bJ2^{-d})^{-1}\) below the square boundary, \((1+bd^2 2^{-d})^{-1}\) at \(J=d\), and \(d^2 2^{-J}/b\) above it. A supported continuous preassignment prior yields the original-record converse while charging the realized finite table; exact endpoint extraction and deterministic shrinkage yield the observable upper bound. The evaluated incidence transition also yields an arbitrary-sequence consistency criterion. Duplicating each block schedule across a group embeds the model in the repeated degree-one neighborhood-interference class and transfers its lower bound. The result supplies a prospective fair, bounded, disjoint-group benchmark for pooling the stable-map replays in the released RUMI synthetic workflow.
